title: Long-form text report
purpose: Clean long-form document: title, summary, key points, sections with callouts, footnotes.
when: Written analysis, memo, proposal, post-mortem, research notes: mostly prose, few numbers.
not_for: Number-heavy pages (use dashboard) or stories with photos (use article).

status.description: Badge, for example draft or final

date.description: Shown in the header, for example 2026-11-01

key_points.description: Bullets in a highlighted box under the summary

body.description: Markdown; may use [^id] footnote references and any artifact-kit fence

callout.description: Optional tinted box after the body

footnotes.description: Notes referenced as [^id] in the text, listed at the end

toc.description: Table of contents when there are 3 or more sections

example.title: Moving the nightly backups to the second server
example.subtitle: A short proposal with the reasoning, the risks and the plan
example.author: Example data
example.summary: Nightly backups run on the main server today and compete with the crawlers for memory between 02:00 and 04:00. Moving them to the second server frees about **3 GB** at peak and shortens the backup window, at the cost of one more SSH hop.
key_points: Peak memory on the main server drops by about 3 GB during the window.
Restore drills stay identical: the archives keep the same names.
One new dependency: the second server to cloud storage link.

sections.heading: Why change anything
sections.body:
The crawlers and the backup runner both peak after midnight. On three nights last week the host fell below the 1 GB free margin[^margin], which is the line we never cross.

The second server has 128 GB and is idle at that hour.

sections.heading: What moves and what stays
sections.body:
| Piece | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| Database dumps | main server | second server |
| File archives | main server | second server |
| Restore drill | main server | main server |

The restore drill stays on the main server on purpose, so a restore still proves the archive is readable from a second machine.

callout.text: No change for anyone who restores: the archive names and the drive folders stay the same.

sections.heading: Risks
sections.body:
- The second server upload link becomes part of the backup path.
- A failed run is now reported from another host; the alert route must follow[^alerts].

callout.text: Keep the old timer disabled, not deleted, for two weeks.

sections.heading: Plan
sections.body:
1. Copy the runner and its unit to the second server.
2. Run both in parallel for three nights and compare the archives.
3. Disable the main server timer.

footnotes.text: Estate rule: keep at least 1 GB RAM and one thread free on every host.
The uptime monitor already runs on the second server, so the alert stays local.
